subject: bat
reasoning:
I'm planning a bat model — skeleton-based with a separate jaw, wings extended in rest pose, aiming for roughly a 0.45m wingspan and 0.1m body length, keeping the design compact but detailed.

I'm working out the joint hierarchy: hips as root with a spine chain up to the chest, then neck, head, and jaw joints, plus ears, fangs, and small eye/nose details. For the wings I'm placing shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints on each side to form the arm chains that will support the wing membranes.

Still placing wing geometry...

Thin slab thickness should stay tiny since planarity is approximate. For the fingers, I'll build two-joint chains from wrist through a midpoint to each tip, sweeping thin tapered tubes along each with a small number of sides for a slender look. For the arm, I'm setting up a chain from shoulder to elbow to wrist to continue the limb rig.

Adding more joint chains...

Working out the tail chain and interfemoral membrane now, adding a short two-span tail behind the hips and a slab polygon connecting the ankles and tail tip to form the stretched skin between the legs.

Then I'm planning the body: sweeping a tapered tube along the spine chain with a lumpy radius profile, applying fur coloring via a countershade paint, and attaching a small sphere for the head bone.

Adding snout, muzzle, nose leaf, and extruded ear shapes with inner pink detailing, plus neck and jaw joints...

Placing facial details next: teeth as tiny cones for fangs, dark sphere eyes with highlights, nose pad, and skipping a noseleaf in favor of a simple pink nose. Then I'm positioning the ears off the head bone.

Now I'm working out the wing membrane coloring using a dark gradient paint from body to wingtip for a leathery look, and defining the finger bone chain with wrist and tip coordinates for each of the four fingers plus thumb.

Finishing the wing geometry with shoulder-elbow-wrist arm segments and midpoint joints with a slight droop, giving a wingspan suited to a fruit bat-like creature, then starting on the membrane panels including the small propatagium triangle near the shoulder.

I'm tracing out the body panel as a simple closed polygon from wrist through finger5, ankle, hip, shoulder, elbow, and back, assigning the wrist bone to drive the finger panels while the elbow bone handles the body panel. For fill, I'm planning to keep things simple with alternating flat colors rather than gradients.

Now I'm working out small details: adding thumb claws via a short rod-and-spike chain off the wrist, and toe spikes swept along each leg chain at the foot tip.

I'm defining the mirrored leg chain geometry with hip, knee, ankle and toe joints, sweeping a tapering radius along it, and placing small forward-pointing toe spikes with tiny radii so the bottoms sit just above the ground plane.

Now I'm setting up the uropatagium slab to attach at the ankle and slope up toward the tail, then building the tail as a simple three-point polyline chain, and starting the spine chain rooted at the hip anchor running up through two spine joints into the chest.

Still designing body parts...

That looks good overall. Now I'll finalize the metadata and write out the complete code.
